description: Rotated binary search indexer compares mid against left element instead of right boundary, failing on unrotated and rotated arrays.
spec_notes: RotatedIndexer.find_pivot_index must compare nums[mid] > nums[right] to find pivot.

tests.test_rotated_search.py:
from search import SearchService
from indexer import RotatedIndexer


def test_standard_rotated_array():
    nums = [4, 5, 6, 7, 1, 2, 3]
    idx = RotatedIndexer(nums)
    assert idx.find_pivot_index() == 4
    assert SearchService.find_minimum_value(nums) == 1


def test_unrotated_sorted_array():
    nums = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
    idx = RotatedIndexer(nums)
    assert idx.find_pivot_index() == 0
    assert SearchService.find_minimum_value(nums) == 1


def test_two_element_rotation():
    nums = [3, 1]
    idx = RotatedIndexer(nums)
    assert idx.find_pivot_index() == 1
    assert SearchService.find_minimum_value(nums) == 1


def test_pivot_at_last_element():
    nums = [2, 3, 4, 5, 1]
    idx = RotatedIndexer(nums)
    assert idx.find_pivot_index() == 4
    assert SearchService.find_minimum_value(nums) == 1


def test_single_element_array():
    nums = [42]
    idx = RotatedIndexer(nums)
    assert idx.find_pivot_index() == 0
    assert SearchService.find_minimum_value(nums) == 42


def test_empty_array():
    idx = RotatedIndexer([])
    assert idx.find_pivot_index() == -1
    assert SearchService.find_minimum_value([]) == -1
